title: Panic and Wonder: How Humanity Reacts to the New and the Unknown
description: A chronological catalog of how humanity has reacted to new technologies, natural events, economic change, prophecies and fiction, from antiquity to 2026: the fears, real and imagined, and the wonder, hope, cooperation and complacency alongside them.

kinds.label: Technology
kinds.description: A weapon, machine, substance or system people built.

kinds.label: Natural
kinds.description: Disasters, pandemics and threats from space.

kinds.label: Economic
kinds.description: Fears that technology would destroy work, or that civilisation would run out of a vital resource.

kinds.label: Social
kinds.description: Moral panics that a medium or technology would corrupt people or society.

kinds.label: Prophecy
kinds.description: Religious, astrological or pseudo-scientific predictions of the end of the world.

kinds.label: Fiction
kinds.description: Novels, films and broadcasts that shaped real fears or policy.

reactions.label: Credible concern
reactions.description: A fear taken seriously by experts or influential thinkers at the time, or a real event with global stakes or mass harm.

reactions.label: Panic
reactions.description: Fear that ran well ahead of the evidence, even where some real harm occurred.

reactions.label: Wonder
reactions.description: Awe at a discovery, sight or achievement.

reactions.label: Optimism
reactions.description: Belief that a technology would transform life for the better, including hype and bubbles.

reactions.label: Cooperation
reactions.description: Nations, scientists or the public working together to meet a threat or a goal.

reactions.label: Humour
reactions.description: Mockery or parties in the face of predicted doom.

reactions.label: Complacency
reactions.description: Overconfidence that a technology or situation was safe.

events.title: Plague of Athens
events.description: An epidemic struck Athens early in the Peloponnesian War, when victory still seemed within reach.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An epidemic struck Athens early in the Peloponnesian War, when victory still seemed within reach.

events.title: Plato on writing
events.description: In the Phaedrus, King Thamus warns that the new technology of writing will weaken people's memory.
events.descriptionMarkdown: In the *Phaedrus*, King Thamus warns that the new technology of writing will weaken people's memory.

events.title: Aristotle on self-working machines
events.description: Aristotle speculated that sufficiently advanced machines would end the need for human labour.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Aristotle speculated that sufficiently advanced machines would end the need for human labour.

events.title: Vespasian blocks a labour-saving device
events.description: The emperor refused a cheap way of hauling heavy goods to protect hauliers' livelihoods.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The emperor refused a cheap way of hauling heavy goods to protect hauliers' livelihoods.

events.title: Antonine Plague
events.description: Smallpox or measles killed 5–10 million, a quarter to a third of the Roman population.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Smallpox or measles killed 5–10 million, a quarter to a third of the Roman population.

events.title: Jian'an Plague
events.description: An epidemic of uncertain cause killed about 2 million in Han dynasty China.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An epidemic of uncertain cause killed about 2 million in Han dynasty China.

events.title: Plague of Justinian
events.description: The first plague pandemic, recurring from the 6th to the 8th century.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The first plague pandemic, recurring from the 6th to the 8th century.

events.title: Japanese smallpox epidemic
events.description: Smallpox killed about a third of Japan's population.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Smallpox killed about a third of Japan's population.

events.title: Millennium fears
events.description: Later writers claimed Christian Europe expected the world to end in the year 1000; historians dispute how widespread the fear was.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Later writers claimed Christian Europe expected the world to end in the year 1000; historians dispute how widespread the fear was.

events.title: Song gunpowder controls
events.description: Song China banned private trade in saltpetre and sulphur, then barred border regions from selling them to foreigners.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Song China banned private trade in saltpetre and sulphur, then barred border regions from selling them to foreigners.

events.title: Black Death
events.description: The worst outbreak of the second plague pandemic, which recurred until the early 19th century.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The worst outbreak of the second plague pandemic, which recurred until the early 19th century.

events.title: Printing press
events.description: Gutenberg's movable-type press spread across Europe within decades; admirers hailed it as a divine gift, though some worried about a flood of books.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Gutenberg's movable-type press spread across Europe within decades; admirers hailed it as a divine gift, though some worried about a flood of books.

events.title: Guild bans on machines
events.description: European authorities often banned labour-saving technologies, sometimes executing those who traded in them.
events.descriptionMarkdown: European authorities often banned labour-saving technologies, sometimes executing those who traded in them.

events.title: Leonardo's withheld diving method
events.description: Leonardo refused to publish how to stay underwater, fearing men would use it to sink ships with their crews.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Leonardo refused to publish how to stay underwater, fearing men would use it to sink ships with their crews.

events.title: Smallpox in Mexico
events.description: Smallpox killed 5–8 million, up to 37% of Mexico's population.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Smallpox killed 5–8 million, up to 37% of Mexico's population.

events.title: Great flood prediction
events.description: Astrologers forecast a world flood from a planetary conjunction; some Europeans moved to high ground or built boats.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Astrologers forecast a world flood from a planetary conjunction; some Europeans moved to high ground or built boats.

events.title: Cocoliztli epidemic
events.description: An epidemic killed an estimated half of Mexico's population.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An epidemic killed an estimated half of Mexico's population.

events.title: Lee's stocking frame
events.description: Elizabeth I refused a patent for a knitting machine, fearing unemployment; James I refused it again.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Elizabeth I refused a patent for a knitting machine, fearing unemployment; James I refused it again.

events.title: Machine breaking
events.description: English weavers destroyed machines that replaced them; by 1727 Parliament made machine-breaking a capital offence.
events.descriptionMarkdown: English weavers destroyed machines that replaced them; by 1727 Parliament made machine-breaking a capital offence.

events.title: Reading mania
events.description: Critics warned that the craze for novels, especially among young women, would corrupt morals and damage health.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Critics warned that the craze for novels, especially among young women, would corrupt morals and damage health.

events.title: Lisbon earthquake
events.description: An earthquake, tsunami and fires destroyed Lisbon, shaking European confidence in a benevolent order.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An earthquake, tsunami and fires destroyed Lisbon, shaking European confidence in a benevolent order.

events.title: Lightning rods and earthquakes
events.description: After the Cape Ann earthquake, Boston minister Thomas Prince blamed Franklin's lightning rods for charging the earth with electricity.
events.descriptionMarkdown: After the Cape Ann earthquake, Boston minister Thomas Prince blamed Franklin's lightning rods for charging the earth with electricity.

events.title: Persian Plague
events.description: Bubonic plague swept Persia.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Bubonic plague swept Persia.

events.title: First balloon flights
events.description: The Montgolfier brothers' hot-air balloon and Jacques Charles's hydrogen balloon drew vast crowds in France.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The Montgolfier brothers' hot-air balloon and Jacques Charles's hydrogen balloon drew vast crowds in France.

events.title: Hydrogen balloon at Gonesse
events.description: Villagers near Paris destroyed Jacques Charles's unmanned balloon with pitchforks and knives.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Villagers near Paris destroyed Jacques Charles's unmanned balloon with pitchforks and knives.

events.title: Laki eruption
events.description: An Icelandic fissure eruption spread a toxic "dry fog" over much of the Northern Hemisphere for months.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An Icelandic fissure eruption spread a toxic "dry fog" over much of the Northern Hemisphere for months.

events.title: Smallpox vaccination
events.description: Edward Jenner's cowpox vaccine spread worldwide, though cartoonists showed the vaccinated sprouting cow parts.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Edward Jenner's cowpox vaccine spread worldwide, though cartoonists showed the vaccinated sprouting cow parts.

events.title: Malthus on population
events.description: Thomas Malthus argued that population growth would always outrun food supply, bringing famine and misery.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Thomas Malthus argued that population growth would always outrun food supply, bringing famine and misery.

events.title: Luddites
events.description: English textile workers disabled knitting frames and looms they believed were destroying their trades.
events.descriptionMarkdown: English textile workers disabled knitting frames and looms they believed were destroying their trades.

events.title: Tambora and the Year Without a Summer
events.titleMarkdown: Tambora and the Year Without a Summer
events.description: The biggest eruption in recent centuries caused crop-killing frosts in North America, famine in Europe, and floods and cholera in India.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The biggest eruption in recent centuries caused crop-killing frosts in North America, famine in Europe, and floods and cholera in India.

events.title: Frankenstein
events.description: Mary Shelley's novel about a scientist's creature became the archetype of science escaping its maker's control.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Mary Shelley's novel about a scientist's creature became the archetype of science escaping its maker's control.

events.title: Ricardo's "On Machinery"
events.description: The leading economist of his age conceded that machinery could cause long-term unemployment.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The leading economist of his age conceded that machinery could cause long-term unemployment.

events.title: Swing Riots
events.description: Farm labourers in southern England smashed threshing machines that were taking their winter work.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Farm labourers in southern England smashed threshing machines that were taking their winter work.

events.title: Railway fears
events.description: Doctors described "siderodromophobia": fever after journeys and agitation at the mere sight of a locomotive.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Doctors described "siderodromophobia": fever after journeys and agitation at the mere sight of a locomotive.

events.title: Biela's Comet
events.description: Reports that the comet would cross Earth's orbit caused alarm in France, though Earth was far away at the time.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Reports that the comet would cross Earth's orbit caused alarm in France, though Earth was far away at the time.

events.title: Millerites
events.description: William Miller's followers expected Christ's return on 22 October 1844; its failure became known as the Great Disappointment.
events.descriptionMarkdown: William Miller's followers expected Christ's return on 22 October 1844; its failure became known as the Great Disappointment.

events.title: "What hath God wrought"
events.description: Samuel Morse sent the first long-distance telegraph message from Washington to Baltimore.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Samuel Morse sent the first long-distance telegraph message from Washington to Baltimore.

events.title: Railway mania
events.description: Britain poured money into hundreds of speculative railway schemes; the bubble burst, ruining many investors but leaving a national network.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Britain poured money into hundreds of speculative railway schemes; the bubble burst, ruining many investors but leaving a national network.

events.title: Great Exhibition
events.description: Millions visited the Crystal Palace in London to see the machines and inventions of the industrial age.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Millions visited the Crystal Palace in London to see the machines and inventions of the industrial age.

events.title: Xhosa cattle-killing
events.description: Prophet Nongqawuse foretold the dead rising and the British being swept away if the Xhosa killed their cattle; the resulting famine killed tens of thousands.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Prophet Nongqawuse foretold the dead rising and the British being swept away if the Xhosa killed their cattle; the resulting famine killed tens of thousands.

events.title: Comet of 1857
events.description: Predictions that a comet would strike Earth in June led to panic in parts of Europe.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Predictions that a comet would strike Earth in June led to panic in parts of Europe.

events.title: Transatlantic telegraph cable
events.description: Queen Victoria and President Buchanan exchanged messages, New York's celebratory fireworks set City Hall alight, and the cable failed within weeks.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Queen Victoria and President Buchanan exchanged messages, New York's celebratory fireworks set City Hall alight, and the cable failed within weeks.

events.title: Carrington Event
events.description: The strongest geomagnetic storm on record caused sparks and fires in telegraph stations worldwide.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The strongest geomagnetic storm on record caused sparks and fires in telegraph stations worldwide.

events.title: Darwin among the Machines
events.description: Samuel Butler, writing in New Zealand's Press, suggested machines might evolve to supplant humans.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Samuel Butler, writing in New Zealand's *Press*, suggested machines might evolve to supplant humans.

events.title: The Coal Question
events.description: William Stanley Jevons warned that exhausting coal would end Britain's industrial supremacy.
events.descriptionMarkdown: William Stanley Jevons warned that exhausting coal would end Britain's industrial supremacy.

events.title: Red Flag Act
events.description: Britain required road locomotives to be preceded by a person on foot, limiting them to walking pace in towns.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Britain required road locomotives to be preceded by a person on foot, limiting them to walking pace in towns.

events.title: Dime novels
events.description: Cheap novels were accused of overstimulating young readers' minds.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Cheap novels were accused of overstimulating young readers' minds.

events.title: Telephone at the Centennial
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell demonstrated his telephone at the Philadelphia Centennial Exhibition, astonishing visitors including Brazil's emperor Pedro II.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Alexander Graham Bell demonstrated his telephone at the Philadelphia Centennial Exhibition, astonishing visitors including Brazil's emperor Pedro II.

events.title: Woosung railway
events.description: Built in Shanghai without Qing approval, China's first railway was bought and dismantled within a year.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Built in Shanghai without Qing approval, China's first railway was bought and dismantled within a year.

events.title: November 1882 solar storm
events.description: A smaller successor to the Carrington Event disrupted telegraph networks.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A smaller successor to the Carrington Event disrupted telegraph networks.

events.title: Krakatoa
events.description: The Indonesian eruption killed tens of thousands and dimmed and coloured skies around the world.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The Indonesian eruption killed tens of thousands and dimmed and coloured skies around the world.

events.title: Electric wire panic
events.description: Amid Edison's campaign against AC, lineman John Feeks's public electrocution sparked a New York panic over overhead wires.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Amid Edison's campaign against AC, lineman John Feeks's public electrocution sparked a New York panic over overhead wires.

events.title: 1889–1890 pandemic
events.description: Influenza or a coronavirus killed about a million people worldwide.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Influenza or a coronavirus killed about a million people worldwide.

events.title: Ghost Dance
events.description: A Paiute prophet's vision of world renewal spread among Plains nations; US alarm at the movement ended in the Wounded Knee massacre.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A Paiute prophet's vision of world renewal spread among Plains nations; US alarm at the movement ended in the Wounded Knee massacre.

events.title: Bicycle face
events.description: Doctors warned that cycling, especially for women, would cause exhaustion and a permanent strained expression.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Doctors warned that cycling, especially for women, would cause exhaustion and a permanent strained expression.

events.title: Bicycle craze
events.description: Cycling became a mass craze; Susan B. Anthony said the bicycle had done more to emancipate women than anything else.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Cycling became a mass craze; Susan B. Anthony said the bicycle had done more to emancipate women than anything else.

events.title: The White City
events.description: Chicago's World's Columbian Exposition was lit by tens of thousands of electric lamps, showcasing an electrified future.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Chicago's World's Columbian Exposition was lit by tens of thousands of electric lamps, showcasing an electrified future.

events.title: First cinema screenings
events.description: The Lumière brothers projected films to paying audiences in Paris; tales of viewers fleeing an oncoming train are probably legend.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The Lumière brothers projected films to paying audiences in Paris; tales of viewers fleeing an oncoming train are probably legend.

events.title: X-ray privacy scare
events.description: Soon after X-rays were discovered, fears that they could see through clothing led to sales of "X-ray-proof" underwear.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Soon after X-rays were discovered, fears that they could see through clothing led to sales of "X-ray-proof" underwear.

events.title: Radium craze
events.description: Radium was sold in tonics, cosmetics and spa water as a cure-all, until poisonings such as the Radium Girls' exposed its dangers.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Radium was sold in tonics, cosmetics and spa water as a cure-all, until poisonings such as the Radium Girls' exposed its dangers.

events.title: Atomic bombs foreseen
events.description: Soddy proposed an atomic bomb to the Royal Engineers; H.G. Wells's The World Set Free predicted atomic warfare.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Soddy proposed an atomic bomb to the Royal Engineers; H.G. Wells's *The World Set Free* predicted atomic warfare.

events.title: Tunguska
events.description: An airburst over Siberia flattened forest across the largest impact area in recorded history.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An airburst over Siberia flattened forest across the largest impact area in recorded history.

events.title: Blériot crosses the Channel
events.description: Louis Blériot's flight thrilled crowds, while British newspapers warned Britain was no longer an island.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Louis Blériot's flight thrilled crowds, while British newspapers warned Britain was no longer an island.

events.title: Halley's Comet
events.description: Cyanogen in the comet's tail led people to seal their windows and buy anti-comet pills, while others threw comet parties.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Cyanogen in the comet's tail led people to seal their windows and buy anti-comet pills, while others threw comet parties.

events.title: Titanic
events.description: A liner widely described as practically unsinkable carried lifeboats for only about half those aboard; over 1,500 died.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A liner widely described as practically unsinkable carried lifeboats for only about half those aboard; over 1,500 died.

events.title: Poison gas at Ypres
events.description: Germany's chlorine attack was the first large-scale use of chemical weapons, later banned by the 1925 Geneva Protocol.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Germany's chlorine attack was the first large-scale use of chemical weapons, later banned by the 1925 Geneva Protocol.

events.title: Spanish flu
events.description: Influenza killed 17–100 million, up to 5.4% of the world's population.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Influenza killed 17–100 million, up to 5.4% of the world's population.

events.title: Radio boom
events.description: Hundreds of broadcast stations appeared within a few years, amid hopes that radio would educate and unite nations.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Hundreds of broadcast stations appeared within a few years, amid hopes that radio would educate and unite nations.

events.title: R.U.R.
events.description: Karel Čapek's Czech play imagined robots destroying the entire human race but one survivor.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Karel Čapek's Czech play imagined robots destroying the entire human race but one survivor.

events.title: May 1921 solar storm
events.description: One of the strongest storms of the 20th century disrupted telegraph and telephone systems.
events.descriptionMarkdown: One of the strongest storms of the 20th century disrupted telegraph and telephone systems.

events.title: Churchill's orange-sized bomb
events.description: Churchill wondered if a bomb no bigger than an orange could destroy a whole block of buildings.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Churchill wondered if a bomb no bigger than an orange could destroy a whole block of buildings.

events.title: Leaded petrol
events.description: Refinery workers died of "loony gas" poisoning before tetraethyl lead went into worldwide use.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Refinery workers died of "loony gas" poisoning before tetraethyl lead went into worldwide use.

events.title: Lindbergh's flight
events.description: Charles Lindbergh's solo transatlantic flight drew huge crowds in Paris and a ticker-tape parade in New York.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Charles Lindbergh's solo transatlantic flight drew huge crowds in Paris and a ticker-tape parade in New York.

events.title: Keynes on technological unemployment
events.description: Keynes popularised the term, calling it "only a temporary phase of maladjustment".
events.descriptionMarkdown: Keynes popularised the term, calling it "only a temporary phase of maladjustment".

events.title: Dust Bowl
events.description: Drought and intensive ploughing turned the US Great Plains into dust storms that drove hundreds of thousands from their farms.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Drought and intensive ploughing turned the US Great Plains into dust storms that drove hundreds of thousands from their farms.

events.title: Comic books
events.description: Comics were blamed for corrupting young people, peaking with Seduction of the Innocent.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Comics were blamed for corrupting young people, peaking with *Seduction of the Innocent*.

events.title: "The bomber will always get through"
events.description: Stanley Baldwin warned Parliament that no defence could stop bombers from devastating cities.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Stanley Baldwin warned Parliament that no defence could stop bombers from devastating cities.

events.title: Chain reaction conceived
events.description: Leó Szilárd conceived the nuclear chain reaction while crossing a London street, and patented it in 1934.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Leó Szilárd conceived the nuclear chain reaction while crossing a London street, and patented it in 1934.

events.title: The War of the Worlds broadcast
events.description: Orson Welles's radio drama was reported to have caused mass panic; historians now think the panic was greatly exaggerated.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Orson Welles's radio drama was reported to have caused mass panic; historians now think the panic was greatly exaggerated.

events.title: Fission discovered
events.description: Hahn and Strassmann split uranium; the Einstein–Szilárd letter led Roosevelt to start work on a bomb.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Hahn and Strassmann split uranium; the Einstein–Szilárd letter led Roosevelt to start work on a bomb.

events.title: "The World of Tomorrow"
events.description: The New York World's Fair promised a future of superhighways, television and plenty, even as war broke out in Europe.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The New York World's Fair promised a future of superhighways, television and plenty, even as war broke out in Europe.

events.title: Unit 731 germ attacks
events.description: Japanese planes dropped plague-infected fleas on Chinese cities including Ningbo and Changde, killing tens of thousands.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Japanese planes dropped plague-infected fleas on Chinese cities including Ningbo and Changde, killing tens of thousands.

events.title: Atmospheric ignition
events.description: Teller raised the risk that a bomb could ignite the atmosphere; the LA-602 report ruled it out, but stayed classified until 1973.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Teller raised the risk that a bomb could ignite the atmosphere; the LA-602 report ruled it out, but stayed classified until 1973.

events.title: Pinball ban
events.description: New York banned pinball as a gambling racket that corrupted youth; police smashed machines, and the ban lasted until 1976.
events.descriptionMarkdown: New York banned pinball as a gambling racket that corrupted youth; police smashed machines, and the ban lasted until 1976.

events.title: Penicillin
events.description: Mass-produced in time for D-Day, the "miracle drug" transformed the treatment of infections, and Fleming shared a Nobel Prize in 1945.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Mass-produced in time for D-Day, the "miracle drug" transformed the treatment of infections, and Fleming shared a Nobel Prize in 1945.

events.title: Trinity, Hiroshima and Nagasaki
events.description: The first nuclear test in July was followed by the bombing of two Japanese cities in August.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The first nuclear test in July was followed by the bombing of two Japanese cities in August.

events.title: Television
events.description: Widespread fears that children were becoming addicted to TV.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Widespread fears that children were becoming addicted to TV.

events.title: Doomsday Clock
events.description: The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists began showing how close humanity stood to self-destruction as minutes to midnight.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The *Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists* began showing how close humanity stood to self-destruction as minutes to midnight.

events.title: Soviet bomb
events.description: The USSR's first atomic test ended the US monopoly.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The USSR's first atomic test ended the US monopoly.

events.title: Cobalt bomb
events.description: On a Chicago radio programme, Szilárd warned that salted H-bombs could annihilate mankind.
events.descriptionMarkdown: On a Chicago radio programme, Szilárd warned that salted H-bombs could annihilate mankind.

events.title: Water fluoridation
events.description: Adding fluoride to public water supplies was cast as mass poisoning or a communist plot.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Adding fluoride to public water supplies was cast as mass poisoning or a communist plot.

events.title: Civil defence
events.description: Truman created the Federal Civil Defense Administration and a national alert network against Soviet attack.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Truman created the Federal Civil Defense Administration and a national alert network against Soviet attack.

events.title: Chalk River
events.description: The first accident at a nuclear reactor, in Canada.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The first accident at a nuclear reactor, in Canada.

events.title: First British bomb and first H-bomb
events.titleMarkdown: First British bomb and first H-bomb
events.description: Britain tested off Western Australia in October; the US tested the first fusion bomb, Ivy Mike, weeks later.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Britain tested off Western Australia in October; the US tested the first fusion bomb, Ivy Mike, weeks later.

events.title: Great Smog of London
events.description: Coal smoke trapped over London for five days killed thousands and led to the Clean Air Act.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Coal smoke trapped over London for five days killed thousands and led to the Clean Air Act.

events.title: Soviet H-bomb
events.description: The USSR tested its first hydrogen bomb, a deliverable design.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The USSR tested its first hydrogen bomb, a deliverable design.

events.title: Atoms for Peace
events.description: Eisenhower told the UN that nuclear technology should serve peaceful ends, leading to the International Atomic Energy Agency in 1957.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Eisenhower told the UN that nuclear technology should serve peaceful ends, leading to the International Atomic Energy Agency in 1957.

events.title: Castle Bravo
events.description: A US H-bomb gave almost three times its expected yield, the worst radiological disaster in US history; its fallout sickened a Japanese fishing crew.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A US H-bomb gave almost three times its expected yield, the worst radiological disaster in US history; its fallout sickened a Japanese fishing crew.

events.title: Godzilla
events.description: Released months after Castle Bravo, Japan's film about a monster awakened by H-bomb tests channelled the country's fear of fallout.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Released months after Castle Bravo, Japan's film about a monster awakened by H-bomb tests channelled the country's fear of fallout.

events.title: "Too cheap to meter"
events.description: The head of the US Atomic Energy Commission predicted electricity too cheap to meter; nuclear power proved expensive.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The head of the US Atomic Energy Commission predicted electricity too cheap to meter; nuclear power proved expensive.

events.title: The Seekers
events.description: A Chicago group awaited rescue by flying saucer before a predicted world flood; its failure inspired the study When Prophecy Fails.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A Chicago group awaited rescue by flying saucer before a predicted world flood; its failure inspired the study *When Prophecy Fails*.

events.title: Russell–Einstein Manifesto
events.description: Eleven eminent scientists warned that H-bomb war might end the human race; it led to the Pugwash conferences in 1957.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Eleven eminent scientists warned that H-bomb war might end the human race; it led to the Pugwash conferences in 1957.

events.title: Automation hearings
events.description: The US Congress held hearings on whether automation would cause mass unemployment.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The US Congress held hearings on whether automation would cause mass unemployment.

events.title: Salk polio vaccine
events.description: When the vaccine was declared safe and effective, church bells rang and people celebrated in the streets.
events.descriptionMarkdown: When the vaccine was declared safe and effective, church bells rang and people celebrated in the streets.

events.title: Minamata disease
events.description: Methylmercury from a Chisso chemical plant poisoned people eating fish from Minamata Bay, Japan.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Methylmercury from a Chisso chemical plant poisoned people eating fish from Minamata Bay, Japan.

events.title: Suez nuclear threats
events.description: The Soviet Union threatened nuclear strikes on Britain and France during the Suez Crisis.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The Soviet Union threatened nuclear strikes on Britain and France during the Suez Crisis.

events.title: Maralinga tests
events.description: Britain tested nuclear weapons at Maralinga in South Australia, ending in 1957.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Britain tested nuclear weapons at Maralinga in South Australia, ending in 1957.

events.title: Kirtland bomb drop
events.description: A nuclear bomb fell from a B-36 near Albuquerque; its conventional explosives detonated, but its nuclear core had been removed.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A nuclear bomb fell from a B-36 near Albuquerque; its conventional explosives detonated, but its nuclear core had been removed.

events.title: On the Beach
events.description: Nevil Shute's novel, set in Melbourne as fallout spreads south after a nuclear war, became a bestseller and a 1959 film.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Nevil Shute's novel, set in Melbourne as fallout spreads south after a nuclear war, became a bestseller and a 1959 film.

events.title: Sputnik and the missile gap
events.description: A Soviet ICBM test and Sputnik fuelled fears of a "missile gap" that later proved an overestimate.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A Soviet ICBM test and Sputnik fuelled fears of a "missile gap" that later proved an overestimate.

events.title: Kyshtym disaster
events.description: A radioactive waste tank exploded at the Soviet Mayak plant; estimates start at more than 200 deaths.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A radioactive waste tank exploded at the Soviet Mayak plant; estimates start at more than 200 deaths.

events.title: Windscale fire
events.description: A British reactor fire spread contamination across the UK and Europe; the inquiry was suppressed.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A British reactor fire spread contamination across the UK and Europe; the inquiry was suppressed.

events.title: Asian flu
events.description: An H2N2 influenza pandemic killed 1–4 million worldwide.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An H2N2 influenza pandemic killed 1–4 million worldwide.

events.title: International Geophysical Year
events.description: Scientists from 67 countries studied the Earth together, launching satellites and starting the Mauna Loa carbon dioxide record.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Scientists from 67 countries studied the Earth together, launching satellites and starting the Mauna Loa carbon dioxide record.

events.title: Tybee Island bomb
events.description: A US bomber jettisoned a nuclear bomb off Georgia after a mid-air collision; it was never recovered.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A US bomber jettisoned a nuclear bomb off Georgia after a mid-air collision; it was never recovered.

events.title: Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament
events.description: CND formed in Britain amid growing fear of nuclear war.
events.descriptionMarkdown: CND formed in Britain amid growing fear of nuclear war.

events.title: Antarctic Treaty
events.description: Twelve nations, including the US and USSR, reserved Antarctica for science and banned military activity and nuclear tests there.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Twelve nations, including the US and USSR, reserved Antarctica for science and banned military activity and nuclear tests there.

events.title: Ignition fears go public
events.description: A magazine article by Pearl Buck revealed the Manhattan Project's atmosphere-ignition worries, alarming readers years after they had been ruled out.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A magazine article by Pearl Buck revealed the Manhattan Project's atmosphere-ignition worries, alarming readers years after they had been ruled out.

events.title: Green Revolution
events.description: High-yield wheat and rice varieties transformed harvests in India, Mexico and beyond; Norman Borlaug won the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize.
events.descriptionMarkdown: High-yield wheat and rice varieties transformed harvests in India, Mexico and beyond; Norman Borlaug won the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize.

events.title: French test in the Sahara
events.description: France tested its first atomic bomb near Reggane in French Algeria.
events.descriptionMarkdown: France tested its first atomic bomb near Reggane in French Algeria.

events.title: Nigeria cuts ties with France
events.description: Protests across Africa against French tests in the Sahara led Nigeria to break off diplomatic relations.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Protests across Africa against French tests in the Sahara led Nigeria to break off diplomatic relations.

events.title: SL-1 accident
events.description: A US Army experimental reactor went prompt critical, killing its three-man crew.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A US Army experimental reactor went prompt critical, killing its three-man crew.

events.title: Goldsboro B-52 crash
events.description: A bomber broke up over North Carolina, dropping two hydrogen bombs; one came close to detonating.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A bomber broke up over North Carolina, dropping two hydrogen bombs; one came close to detonating.

events.title: Gagarin's flight
events.description: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space, and huge crowds greeted him in Moscow.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space, and huge crowds greeted him in Moscow.

events.title: K-19 submarine accident
events.description: A reactor coolant failure on a Soviet nuclear submarine, with Vasili Arkhipov aboard, killed several crew.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A reactor coolant failure on a Soviet nuclear submarine, with Vasili Arkhipov aboard, killed several crew.

events.title: Thalidomide
events.description: A sedative given to pregnant women was withdrawn after causing birth defects in thousands of children, reshaping drug regulation.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A sedative given to pregnant women was withdrawn after causing birth defects in thousands of children, reshaping drug regulation.

events.title: Checkpoint Charlie standoff
events.description: US and Soviet tanks faced off in Berlin until Kennedy and Khrushchev negotiated their withdrawal.
events.descriptionMarkdown: US and Soviet tanks faced off in Berlin until Kennedy and Khrushchev negotiated their withdrawal.

events.title: Tsar Bomba and the test ban
events.titleMarkdown: Tsar Bomba and the test ban
events.description: The USSR detonated the most powerful bomb ever; in 1963 the Partial Test Ban Treaty moved tests underground.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The USSR detonated the most powerful bomb ever; in 1963 the Partial Test Ban Treaty moved tests underground.

events.title: Project West Ford
events.description: Radio astronomers protested a US ring of orbiting copper needles, and Pravda ran the headline "U.S.A. Dirties Space".
events.descriptionMarkdown: Radio astronomers protested a US ring of orbiting copper needles, and *Pravda* ran the headline "U.S.A. Dirties Space".

events.title: Seventh cholera pandemic
events.description: A still-ongoing cholera pandemic has killed an estimated 1.4–9.3 million.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A still-ongoing cholera pandemic has killed an estimated 1.4–9.3 million.

events.title: Mexico City radiation accident
events.description: An orphaned cobalt-60 source from a radiography device killed four people.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An orphaned cobalt-60 source from a radiography device killed four people.

events.title: Starfish Prime
events.description: A high-altitude US test's pulse damaged electrics in Hawaii, disrupted Pacific communications and disabled satellites.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A high-altitude US test's pulse damaged electrics in Hawaii, disrupted Pacific communications and disabled satellites.

events.title: Telstar
events.description: The first live transatlantic television via satellite amazed viewers, and a pop instrumental named after it topped the charts.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The first live transatlantic television via satellite amazed viewers, and a pop instrumental named after it topped the charts.

events.title: Silent Spring
events.description: Rachel Carson's book on DDT launched the modern environmental movement and led to a US DDT ban in 1972.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Rachel Carson's book on DDT launched the modern environmental movement and led to a US DDT ban in 1972.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
events.description: Vasili Arkhipov refused to approve firing a nuclear torpedo from the Soviet submarine B-59.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Vasili Arkhipov refused to approve firing a nuclear torpedo from the Soviet submarine B-59.

events.title: Cat's Cradle
events.description: Kurt Vonnegut's novel imagined "ice-nine", a lab-made substance that freezes all Earth's water, later invoked in the polywater scare.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Kurt Vonnegut's novel imagined "ice-nine", a lab-made substance that freezes all Earth's water, later invoked in the polywater scare.

events.title: Dr. Strangelove and Fail-Safe
events.description: Two films showed nuclear war triggered by a rogue general and by a technical error, satirising and dramatising US strategy.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Two films showed nuclear war triggered by a rogue general and by a technical error, satirising and dramatising US strategy.

events.title: China's first bomb
events.description: China tested an atomic bomb at Lop Nur.
events.descriptionMarkdown: China tested an atomic bomb at Lop Nur.

events.title: Automation scare
events.description: Fears of automation-driven mass unemployment led to a presidential commission, whose 1966 report found no lasting effect.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Fears of automation-driven mass unemployment led to a presidential commission, whose 1966 report found no lasting effect.

events.title: Intelligence explosion
events.description: I.J. Good wrote that the first ultraintelligent machine would be the last invention humans need make.
events.descriptionMarkdown: I.J. Good wrote that the first ultraintelligent machine would be the last invention humans need make.

events.title: Northeast blackout
events.description: US emergency planners mistook a regional blackout for a nuclear attack.
events.descriptionMarkdown: US emergency planners mistook a regional blackout for a nuclear attack.

events.title: The War Game
events.description: The BBC and British government kept a realistic docudrama of nuclear war off air for 20 years; it won an Oscar abroad.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The BBC and British government kept a realistic docudrama of nuclear war off air for 20 years; it won an Oscar abroad.

events.title: Palomares B-52 crash
events.description: A US bomber collided with a tanker over Spain, scattering plutonium from two of its hydrogen bombs.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A US bomber collided with a tanker over Spain, scattering plutonium from two of its hydrogen bombs.

events.title: China's live missile test
events.description: China fired a nuclear-armed missile over populated areas to Lop Nur, the only such test by any country.
events.descriptionMarkdown: China fired a nuclear-armed missile over populated areas to Lop Nur, the only such test by any country.

events.title: Marburg virus
events.description: Lab workers in Germany and Yugoslavia handling monkeys imported from Uganda caught a previously unknown haemorrhagic fever; seven died.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Lab workers in Germany and Yugoslavia handling monkeys imported from Uganda caught a previously unknown haemorrhagic fever; seven died.

events.title: Outer Space Treaty
events.description: The treaty banned nuclear weapons tests in space.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The treaty banned nuclear weapons tests in space.

events.title: Solar storm radar outage
events.description: A solar event knocked out polar surveillance radars, and the US military scrambled for a nuclear attack.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A solar event knocked out polar surveillance radars, and the US military scrambled for a nuclear attack.

events.title: First heart transplant
events.description: Christiaan Barnard's team in Cape Town transplanted a human heart, making headlines around the world.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Christiaan Barnard's team in Cape Town transplanted a human heart, making headlines around the world.

events.title: Thule B-52 crash
events.description: A nuclear-armed US bomber crashed in Greenland, spreading radioactive contamination.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A nuclear-armed US bomber crashed in Greenland, spreading radioactive contamination.

events.title: Non-Proliferation Treaty
events.description: The treaty opened for signature to limit the spread of nuclear weapons.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The treaty opened for signature to limit the spread of nuclear weapons.

events.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
events.description: Kubrick's film, with I.J. Good as a consultant, made HAL 9000 the defining image of a computer turning on its crew.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Kubrick's film, with I.J. Good as a consultant, made HAL 9000 the defining image of a computer turning on its crew.

events.title: The Population Bomb
events.description: Paul Ehrlich predicted mass famines in the 1970s; the Green Revolution's higher yields largely averted them.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Paul Ehrlich predicted mass famines in the 1970s; the Green Revolution's higher yields largely averted them.

events.title: Earthrise
events.description: Apollo 8's photograph of Earth rising over the Moon became an icon of the planet's fragility.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Apollo 8's photograph of Earth rising over the Moon became an icon of the planet's fragility.

events.title: Hong Kong flu
events.description: An H3N2 influenza pandemic killed 1–4 million worldwide.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An H3N2 influenza pandemic killed 1–4 million worldwide.

events.title: The Andromeda Strain
events.description: Michael Crichton's novel about a deadly microbe brought back by a satellite appeared months before the Moon landing.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Michael Crichton's novel about a deadly microbe brought back by a satellite appeared months before the Moon landing.

events.title: Moon landing
events.description: Hundreds of millions watched Apollo 11 land and Neil Armstrong step onto the Moon.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Hundreds of millions watched Apollo 11 land and Neil Armstrong step onto the Moon.

events.title: Apollo 11 quarantine
events.description: Astronauts were quarantined for 21 days in case they brought back lunar microorganisms.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Astronauts were quarantined for 21 days in case they brought back lunar microorganisms.

events.title: Polywater
events.description: A physicist called "anomalous water" the most dangerous material on earth, echoing ice-nine. It proved to be contamination.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A physicist called "anomalous water" the most dangerous material on earth, echoing ice-nine. It proved to be contamination.

events.title: Global cooling scare
events.description: Magazine stories warned of a coming ice age, though most climate research of the time pointed towards warming.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Magazine stories warned of a coming ice age, though most climate research of the time pointed towards warming.

events.title: Killer bees
events.description: Africanised honeybees that escaped from a Brazilian research programme in 1957 spread north, provoking alarm and horror films in the US.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Africanised honeybees that escaped from a Brazilian research programme in 1957 spread north, provoking alarm and horror films in the US.

events.title: Violent video games
events.description: Games were blamed for making children violent, on the strength of later-discredited theories.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Games were blamed for making children violent, on the strength of later-discredited theories.

events.title: Earth Day
events.description: About 20 million Americans joined the first Earth Day, and new environmental laws and agencies followed.
events.descriptionMarkdown: About 20 million Americans joined the first Earth Day, and new environmental laws and agencies followed.

events.title: Supersonic transport and ozone
events.description: Harold Johnston warned that exhaust from a proposed supersonic fleet could damage the ozone layer.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Harold Johnston warned that exhaust from a proposed supersonic fleet could damage the ozone layer.

events.title: The Limits to Growth
events.description: The Club of Rome's World3 computer model showed "overshoot and collapse" by the late 21st century in two of three scenarios.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The Club of Rome's World3 computer model showed "overshoot and collapse" by the late 21st century in two of three scenarios.

events.title: Biological Weapons Convention
events.description: The first treaty to ban an entire class of weapons opened for signature.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The first treaty to ban an entire class of weapons opened for signature.

events.title: The Blue Marble
events.description: Apollo 17's photograph of the whole sunlit Earth became one of the most reproduced images in history.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Apollo 17's photograph of the whole sunlit Earth became one of the most reproduced images in history.

events.title: Yom Kippur nuclear alert
events.description: Israel considered using nuclear weapons, and Soviet moves put US forces on high alert.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Israel considered using nuclear weapons, and Soviet moves put US forces on high alert.

events.title: Oil crisis
events.description: An Arab oil embargo quadrupled prices, fuelling fears that industrial economies were running out of energy.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An Arab oil embargo quadrupled prices, fuelling fears that industrial economies were running out of energy.

events.title: Japan Sinks
events.description: Sakyo Komatsu's bestselling novel about the Japanese archipelago sinking into the sea tapped the country's fear of earthquakes.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Sakyo Komatsu's bestselling novel about the Japanese archipelago sinking into the sea tapped the country's fear of earthquakes.

events.title: The Prophecies of Nostradamus
events.description: Tsutomu Gotō's bestseller told millions of Japanese readers that Nostradamus foresaw the end of humanity in July 1999.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Tsutomu Gotō's bestseller told millions of Japanese readers that Nostradamus foresaw the end of humanity in July 1999.

events.title: CFCs
events.description: Rowland and Molina predicted that CFCs would release ozone-destroying chlorine in the stratosphere.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Rowland and Molina predicted that CFCs would release ozone-destroying chlorine in the stratosphere.

events.title: India's first nuclear test
events.description: India tested "Smiling Buddha" at Pokhran.
events.descriptionMarkdown: India tested "Smiling Buddha" at Pokhran.

events.title: Recombinant DNA
events.description: Scientists paused gene-splicing experiments over biohazard fears, then set rules at Asilomar.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Scientists paused gene-splicing experiments over biohazard fears, then set rules at Asilomar.

events.title: The Jupiter Effect
events.description: A popular book claimed a 1982 planetary alignment would trigger earthquakes, including on the San Andreas Fault; nothing happened.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A popular book claimed a 1982 planetary alignment would trigger earthquakes, including on the San Andreas Fault; nothing happened.

events.title: Apollo–Soyuz
events.description: US and Soviet spacecraft docked in orbit, and their crews shook hands at the height of détente.
events.descriptionMarkdown: US and Soviet spacecraft docked in orbit, and their crews shook hands at the height of détente.

events.title: Seveso
events.description: A chemical plant accident near Milan released dioxin over nearby towns.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A chemical plant accident near Milan released dioxin over nearby towns.

events.title: Swine flu vaccination
events.description: An outbreak at Fort Dix prompted a rushed US mass vaccination; the feared pandemic never came.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An outbreak at Fort Dix prompted a rushed US mass vaccination; the feared pandemic never came.

events.title: Neutron bomb
events.description: Reports of a US radiation warhead for Europe caused an outcry; Carter cancelled it the next year.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Reports of a US radiation warhead for Europe caused an outcry; Carter cancelled it the next year.

events.title: Russian flu
events.description: An H1N1 strain almost identical to one from the 1950s re-emerged in China and the USSR, pointing to a lab or vaccine-trial origin.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An H1N1 strain almost identical to one from the 1950s re-emerged in China and the USSR, pointing to a lab or vaccine-trial origin.

events.title: Voyager Golden Record
events.description: The two Voyager probes carried records of Earth's sounds, music and greetings in 55 languages for any civilisation that might find them.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The two Voyager probes carried records of Earth's sounds, music and greetings in 55 languages for any civilisation that might find them.

events.title: Kessler syndrome
events.description: NASA's Donald Kessler showed that crowded orbits could trigger a self-sustaining cascade of collisions.
events.descriptionMarkdown: NASA's Donald Kessler showed that crowded orbits could trigger a self-sustaining cascade of collisions.

events.title: Kosmos 954
events.description: A nuclear-powered Soviet satellite crashed in Canada's Northwest Territories.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A nuclear-powered Soviet satellite crashed in Canada's Northwest Territories.

events.title: Birmingham smallpox death
events.description: A photographer caught smallpox from a university lab below her office and became the last person known to die of the disease.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A photographer caught smallpox from a university lab below her office and became the last person known to die of the disease.

events.title: First IVF baby
events.description: Louise Brown's birth in England was hailed as a medical marvel, amid fears of "test-tube babies" and designer children.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Louise Brown's birth in England was hailed as a medical marvel, amid fears of "test-tube babies" and designer children.

events.title: The China Syndrome
events.description: A thriller about a cover-up at a nuclear plant opened 12 days before the Three Mile Island accident.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A thriller about a cover-up at a nuclear plant opened 12 days before the Three Mile Island accident.

events.title: Three Mile Island
events.description: A partial meltdown caused alarm, though regulators found it caused no deaths or injuries.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A partial meltdown caused alarm, though regulators found it caused no deaths or injuries.

events.title: Power lines and cancer
events.description: A study linking power lines to childhood leukaemia started decades of fears about electromagnetic fields.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A study linking power lines to childhood leukaemia started decades of fears about electromagnetic fields.

events.title: Church Rock uranium spill
events.description: A uranium mill spill in New Mexico, on Navajo land, is listed among major radioactive incidents.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A uranium mill spill in New Mexico, on Navajo land, is listed among major radioactive incidents.

events.title: Sverdlovsk anthrax leak
events.description: Anthrax from a Soviet military facility killed at least 64; the USSR blamed tainted meat until Yeltsin admitted the truth in 1992.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Anthrax from a Soviet military facility killed at least 64; the USSR blamed tainted meat until Yeltsin admitted the truth in 1992.

events.title: Skylab re-entry
events.description: As the station fell, Devon holidaymakers planned to shelter in a cave and Brussels readied air-raid sirens; debris landed in Western Australia.
events.descriptionMarkdown: As the station fell, Devon holidaymakers planned to shelter in a cave and Brussels readied air-raid sirens; debris landed in Western Australia.

events.title: Vela incident
events.description: A US satellite recorded a double flash in the South Atlantic, widely believed to be a South African or Israeli nuclear test.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A US satellite recorded a double flash in the South Atlantic, widely believed to be a South African or Israeli nuclear test.

events.title: NORAD false alarm
events.description: A computer glitch showed a Soviet launch, and US forces prepared to retaliate.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A computer glitch showed a Soviet launch, and US forces prepared to retaliate.

events.title: Dungeons & Dragons
events.description: Role-playing games were accused of leading young people into drug use and Satanism.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Role-playing games were accused of leading young people into drug use and Satanism.

events.title: Acid rain
events.description: Sulphur emissions from power stations were blamed for dying lakes and forests; West Germany feared Waldsterben, the death of its forests.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Sulphur emissions from power stations were blamed for dying lakes and forests; West Germany feared *Waldsterben*, the death of its forests.

events.title: Backmasking
events.description: Campaigners claimed rock records hid satanic messages audible only when played backwards.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Campaigners claimed rock records hid satanic messages audible only when played backwards.

events.title: AIDS
events.description: The AIDS pandemic spread worldwide, accompanied by a moral panic aimed particularly at gay men.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The AIDS pandemic spread worldwide, accompanied by a moral panic aimed particularly at gay men.

events.title: Alvarez impact hypothesis
events.description: Luis and Walter Alvarez proposed that an asteroid impact killed the dinosaurs, making impacts a recognised extinction risk.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Luis and Walter Alvarez proposed that an asteroid impact killed the dinosaurs, making impacts a recognised extinction risk.

events.title: Smallpox eradicated
events.description: After a global vaccination campaign spanning Cold War rivals, the World Health Assembly declared smallpox eradicated.
events.descriptionMarkdown: After a global vaccination campaign spanning Cold War rivals, the World Health Assembly declared smallpox eradicated.

events.title: NORAD chip failure
events.description: A faulty computer chip showed Soviet missiles incoming, and US bomber crews were ordered to their aircraft.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A faulty computer chip showed Soviet missiles incoming, and US bomber crews were ordered to their aircraft.

events.title: Damascus Titan II explosion
events.description: A dropped socket punctured a missile's fuel tank in Arkansas; the explosion threw its nuclear warhead clear without detonating it.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A dropped socket punctured a missile's fuel tank in Arkansas; the explosion threw its nuclear warhead clear without detonating it.

events.title: Central Park disarmament rally
events.description: The largest anti-war demonstration in history protested nuclear weapons in New York.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The largest anti-war demonstration in history protested nuclear weapons in New York.

events.title: Low ozone at Syowa
events.description: Japanese scientist Shigeru Chubachi measured unusually low ozone at Syowa station in Antarctica.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Japanese scientist Shigeru Chubachi measured unusually low ozone at Syowa station in Antarctica.

events.title: Video nasties
events.description: British tabloids blamed violent home videos for corrupting children, leading to the Video Recordings Act 1984.
events.descriptionMarkdown: British tabloids blamed violent home videos for corrupting children, leading to the Video Recordings Act 1984.

events.title: Strategic Defense Initiative
events.description: Reagan announced a missile-defence programme against Soviet nuclear attack.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Reagan announced a missile-defence programme against Soviet nuclear attack.

events.title: WarGames
events.description: After watching the film, Reagan asked if it could really happen; the answer led to NSDD-145, an early US computer security policy.
events.descriptionMarkdown: After watching the film, Reagan asked if it could really happen; the answer led to NSDD-145, an early US computer security policy.

events.title: Petrov false alarm
events.description: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov judged a satellite warning of US missiles to be false and did not report it up the chain.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov judged a satellite warning of US missiles to be false and did not report it up the chain.

events.title: Able Archer 83
events.description: The USSR mistook a NATO exercise for preparations for a first strike and put forces on high alert.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The USSR mistook a NATO exercise for preparations for a first strike and put forces on high alert.

events.title: Nuclear winter and The Day After
events.titleMarkdown: Nuclear winter and The Day After
events.description: The TTAPS study raised the prospect of nuclear winter; The Day After and the BBC's Threads shifted public attitudes.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The TTAPS study raised the prospect of nuclear winter; *The Day After* and the BBC's *Threads* shifted public attitudes.

events.title: Bhopal
events.description: A methyl isocyanate leak at a Union Carbide plant in India exposed over 500,000 people and killed at least 3,787.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A methyl isocyanate leak at a Union Carbide plant in India exposed over 500,000 people and killed at least 3,787.

events.title: The Terminator
events.description: James Cameron's film about a defence computer, Skynet, launching nuclear war became the shorthand for AI takeover.
events.descriptionMarkdown: James Cameron's film about a defence computer, Skynet, launching nuclear war became the shorthand for AI takeover.

events.title: Ozone hole
events.description: British Antarctic Survey scientists found a recurring ozone hole, published in 1985; the Montreal Protocol followed in 1987.
events.descriptionMarkdown: British Antarctic Survey scientists found a recurring ozone hole, published in 1985; the Montreal Protocol followed in 1987.

events.title: Rainbow Warrior
events.description: French agents sank a Greenpeace ship in Auckland as it headed to protest nuclear tests at Moruroa.
events.descriptionMarkdown: French agents sank a Greenpeace ship in Auckland as it headed to protest nuclear tests at Moruroa.

events.title: Halley's return
events.description: European, Soviet and Japanese probes flew past the comet together, and Giotto sent back the first close-up of a comet's nucleus.
events.descriptionMarkdown: European, Soviet and Japanese probes flew past the comet together, and Giotto sent back the first close-up of a comet's nucleus.

events.title: Challenger
events.description: The shuttle broke apart after launch; engineers' warnings about its seals in cold weather had been overruled.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The shuttle broke apart after launch; engineers' warnings about its seals in cold weather had been overruled.

events.title: Brain virus
events.description: Two brothers in Pakistan wrote the first IBM PC virus to punish people pirating their software.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Two brothers in Pakistan wrote the first IBM PC virus to punish people pirating their software.

events.title: Chernobyl
events.description: An explosion and fire killed about 31 people directly; long-term death estimates range from 4,000 to 16,000 and are disputed.
events.descriptionMarkdown: An explosion and fire killed about 31 people directly; long-term death estimates range from 4,000 to 16,000 and are disputed.

events.title: Grey goo
events.description: Eric Drexler coined the term for self-replicating nanomachines consuming the biosphere; in 2004 he wished he never had.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Eric Drexler coined the term for self-replicating nanomachines consuming the biosphere; in 2004 he wished he never had.

events.title: Lake Nyos
events.description: A carbon dioxide eruption from a crater lake in Cameroon suffocated 1,746 people.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A carbon dioxide eruption from a crater lake in Cameroon suffocated 1,746 people.

events.title: Goiânia
events.description: A lost radiotherapy source in Brazil exposed 249 people to large doses and killed four.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A lost radiotherapy source in Brazil exposed 249 people to large doses and killed four.

events.title: Black Monday
events.description: Stock markets crashed worldwide, with the Dow falling 22.6% in a day; automated program trading was blamed for deepening the fall.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Stock markets crashed worldwide, with the Dow falling 22.6% in a day; automated program trading was blamed for deepening the fall.

events.title: Hansen's climate testimony
events.description: NASA's James Hansen told the US Senate that human-caused warming had arrived, bringing climate change into mainstream politics.
events.descriptionMarkdown: NASA's James Hansen told the US Senate that human-caused warming had arrived, bringing climate change into mainstream politics.

events.title: Morris worm
events.description: The first major internet worm disrupted an estimated tenth of all connected computers.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The first major internet worm disrupted an estimated tenth of all connected computers.

events.title: AIDS Trojan
events.description: The first known ransomware demanded $189 to decrypt victims' files.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The first known ransomware demanded $189 to decrypt victims' files.

events.title: World Wide Web proposed
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the web at CERN; it was released free for anyone to use in 1993.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the web at CERN; it was released free for anyone to use in 1993.

events.title: Quebec blackout
events.description: A geomagnetic storm knocked out power across the whole province of Quebec for nine hours.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A geomagnetic storm knocked out power across the whole province of Quebec for nine hours.

events.title: Internet moral panic
events.description: Media alarm over online pornography and crime accompanied the internet's spread.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Media alarm over online pornography and crime accompanied the internet's spread.

events.title: Pale Blue Dot
events.description: Voyager 1 photographed Earth from about 6 billion kilometres away as a speck in a sunbeam, at Carl Sagan's urging.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Voyager 1 photographed Earth from about 6 billion kilometres away as a speck in a sunbeam, at Carl Sagan's urging.

events.title: Kuwait oil fires
events.description: Carl Sagan predicted Tambora-like crop failures, especially in South Asia; the effects stayed regional.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Carl Sagan predicted Tambora-like crop failures, especially in South Asia; the effects stayed regional.

events.title: Salyut 7 re-entry
events.description: The 40-tonne Soviet space station fell uncontrolled over Argentina.
events.descriptionMarkdown: The 40-tonne Soviet space station fell uncontrolled over Argentina.

events.title: Michelangelo virus
events.description: A media frenzy predicted machines wiped worldwide on 6 March; the damage was minimal.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A media frenzy predicted machines wiped worldwide on 6 March; the damage was minimal.

events.title: Biopreparat revealed
events.description: Defector Ken Alibek disclosed that the Soviet Union had run a vast secret programme producing weaponised smallpox, anthrax and plague.
events.descriptionMarkdown: Defector Ken Alibek disclosed that the Soviet Union had run a vast secret programme producing weaponised smallpox, anthrax and plague.

events.title: Dami Mission rapture
events.description: A South Korean church predicted the rapture on 28 October; thousands quit jobs and gave away possessions before the date passed.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A South Korean church predicted the rapture on 28 October; thousands quit jobs and gave away possessions before the date passed.

events.title: Mobile phones and brain cancer
events.description: A widower's lawsuit, aired on Larry King Live, set off a wave of suits; he lost for lack of evidence.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A widower's lawsuit, aired on *Larry King Live*, set off a wave of suits; he lost for lack of evidence.

events.title: Shoemaker–Levy 9
events.description: A comet's fragments hit Jupiter with hundreds of times the energy of Earth's nuclear arsenal, and asteroid detection won new funding.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A comet's fragments hit Jupiter with hundreds of times the energy of Earth's nuclear arsenal, and asteroid detection won new funding.

events.title: Surat plague
events.description: A plague outbreak in Surat, India, killed dozens but prompted hundreds of thousands to flee the city and countries to halt flights.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A plague outbreak in Surat, India, killed dozens but prompted hundreds of thousands to flee the city and countries to halt flights.

events.title: Aum Shinrikyo
events.description: A Japanese doomsday cult's sarin attack on the Tokyo subway killed 12; it had also tried anthrax and sent a team to seek Ebola.
events.descriptionMarkdown: A Japanese doomsday cult's sarin attack on the Tokyo subway killed 12; it had also tried anthrax and sent a team to seek Ebola.

events.title: Kikwit Ebola outbreak
events.description: An Ebola outbreak in Zaire killed hundreds and, with the bestseller The Hot Zone, made the virus a global fear.
